summary: Lookout site since 1918; a cathedral-style tower stood 1928-1958, replaced by the present R-6 flattop on a 20-foot tower, staffed until 1973 and now a restored Recreation.gov rental.

facts.status_note: Restored; no longer staffed regularly, used occasionally for emergency fire detection.

access.note: Rentable via Recreation.gov; combination lock, code from McKenzie River Ranger Station.

visit.trail_note: Rocky access road; steep, narrow steps up a 30-foot tower to the cabin.

events.note: Site first developed with an open-sided cupola shelter.
Replaced by a 10x10' 'Firechaser' frame cabin with a 29' third-story cathedral-style observatory.
NHLR says the cathedral-style structure remained in service until 1958 (not maintained afterward; no examples remain).
NHLR dates the present 15'x15' R-6 flattop tower to 1957; firelookout.com and the Recreation.gov listing instead give 1958 for its construction -- sources disagree by one year.
Remained in regular Forest Service fire-detection service until 1973.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register November 24, 1995.

evidence.quote: Indian Ridge has been the site of a lookout since 1918.

evidence.supports: Cathedral-style structure in service until 1958, not maintained, no examples remain
evidence.quote: It is well known as the location of a classic 29' "cathedral style" structure which remained in service until 1958 and regrettably was not maintained. No examples remain.

evidence.supports: Present R-6 flattop built 1957, catwalk, 20' wooden tower
evidence.quote: The present 15'x 15' R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 20' wooden tower was built in 1957 and remained in service until 1973.

evidence.supports: Restored and now in the cabin rental system, occasional emergency use
evidence.quote: It has been restored and is now available in the cabin rental system and is occasionally used for detection on an emergency basis.

evidence.supports: 1918 open-sided cupola shelter; 1928 Firechaser cabin with 29' observatory
evidence.quote: Developed in 1918 with an open-sided cupola shelter, a 10x10' "Firechaser" frame cabin with 29' 3rd story observatory replaced it in 1928.

evidence.supports: Present 20' tower with R-6 cab built 1958
evidence.quote: The present 20' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab, built in 1958, is currently available on the Recreation Rental program.

evidence.supports: Built 1958, staffed until 1973, still used occasionally for emergencies
evidence.quote: Built in 1958, the lookout was used for firefighting by Forest Service personnel until 1973. The lookout is still staffed occasionally during emergencies.

evidence.supports: Rocky access road, steep steps up 30-foot tower, primitive accommodations
evidence.quote: The lookout is accessible by car, although the access road is rocky. Guests must be prepared to climb steep, narrow steps up the 30-foot tower to access the lookout's cabin.

evidence.supports: Sand Mountain and Carpenter Mountain visible, beargrass and huckleberries on ridge
evidence.quote: The Sand Mountain and Carpenter Mountain Lookouts are visible with binoculars.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1957 for the current R-6 tower; firelookout.com and the Recreation.gov listing both give 1958. Story and events note the one-year discrepancy rather than picking a single year.

notes_for_editor: Brief's build year (1957) matches NHLR; firelookout.com/recreation.gov say 1958, so this is a genuine one-year source conflict (noted in the story and resolved_conflicts), not a brief error.
